# Best RV power station and solar combos

The right pick depends on what you run. No single combo is best for every RV. Panels are sold separately from the power stations in most of these sources, so match panel wattage to the station's solar input limit. A panel array bigger than that limit won't charge any faster.

## Weekend or light use (fridge, Starlink, laptops, CPAP)
**Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 plus two SolarSaga 200W panels.**
- It has 1,070Wh, 1,500W output, a 400W solar input limit and weighs about 23.8 lb.
- Two 200W panels use the full 400W input, per [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/).
- The catch is that it can't be expanded with extra batteries.

## Mid-range, with room to grow
**EcoFlow Delta 3 Plus.** [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/) ranks it best overall for camping.
- It has 1,024Wh, 1,800W output and a 1,000W solar input over two 500W inputs. It expands to 5kWh.
- Full solar charging takes about 70 minutes, but only with around 1,000W of panels connected. A single 200W panel works, just slower.

**Bluetti AC200L** is the step up if you want about 2kWh. It has 2,048Wh, 2,400W output, 1,200W solar input and a built-in 30A RV outlet. It weighs about 62 lb. ([Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), [EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))

## Full-time RVing or running the roof AC
- **EcoFlow Delta Pro 3:** 4,096Wh, 4,000W continuous and 8,000W surge. It expands past 12kWh and recharges 0–80% in about 50 minutes. It's heavy, a two-person lift. ([EmergencyEnergy](https://www.emergencyenergy.co/articles/rv-power-station/))
- **Jackery Explorer 3000 Pro:** 3,024Wh and 3,000W, enough to start a 13,500 BTU AC without a soft-start kit, according to the same source.

## A deal I found
**ALLPOWERS R4000** has 3,456Wh, 3,600W at 120V, an RV outlet and up to 2,000W of solar input over three inputs. It carries a 5-year warranty.
- The store price is $1,499. With code EXTRA12 it was $1,319.12 in the store's cart test on Oct 23. The code expires Nov 15, 2026.
- It weighs 45 kg (about 99 lb), so it's not a hand-carry unit.
- Reaching 2,000W of solar needs panels on all three inputs, since each tops out at 650W.
- [Buy at ALLPOWERS](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh). This is an affiliate link, and checkout has the final word on price. ([Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-r4000-3456wh))

## Panels
The only specific panels named in the results were Renogy's 200W Foldable Solar Suitcase and a 100W foldable panel ([NomadSignal](https://nomadsignal.co/blogs/news/jackery-vs-ecoflow-vs-bluetti-vanlife)), plus Jackery SolarSaga panels. I don't have prices or direct links for them. Jackery's pair most easily with Jackery stations.

## Quick sizing
Add up your loads in watts, then multiply by hours. A 150W fridge over 10 hours is about 1,500Wh ([Acquired Sense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html)). Also check the largest startup load, such as the AC, against the station's surge rating.

## Caveats
- I don't have direct purchase links for the Jackery, EcoFlow or Bluetti models, only the review pages. Check current prices on the brands' stores or Amazon.
- These sources are affiliate review sites, and prices and specs vary by listing, so confirm before buying.
- The EmergencyEnergy article covers Ontario rules. In the US, have an electrician handle any hardwired connection to your RV.

Tell me your RV type, whether you need to run the AC, and your budget, and I can narrow this to one combo.
